slides.title: Why Deployment Metrics Matter for AI-Native Pipelines
slides.notes: Explain that AI-native pipelines include model serving, data preprocessing, and inference services. Traditional deployment metrics (CPU, memory) don't capture model drift, prediction latency distributions, or cascade failures. This lecture teaches how to evaluate deployment and reliability metrics for multi-component AI systems, using live scenario walkthroughs.

slides.title: Core Deployment Metrics for Multi-Component Systems

figure.caption: Key deployment metrics and collection methods

slides.notes: Deployment metrics must be collected per component and aggregated. Latency percentiles reveal tail latency issues. Throughput indicates capacity. Error rates categorized by HTTP codes, model errors, timeouts. Rollback frequency shows deployment stability. Resource saturation (CPU, GPU, memory) predicts failures.

slides.title: Reliability Metrics: MTBF, MTTR, Availability, SLOs
slides.notes: Reliability metrics quantify system health over time. MTBF and MTTR are classic. SLOs translate business requirements into measurable targets (e.g., 99.9% requests <200ms). Error budgets allow balancing feature velocity vs reliability. These metrics guide automated deployment decisions.

slides.title: Evaluating Multi-Component Projects: Dependency Mapping
bullets: Identify all services, models, data stores
slides.notes: A multi-component AI project may include data pipelines, feature stores, model servers, and business logic services. Dependency mapping reveals cascading failure risks. Contract tests ensure compatibility. Distributed tracing (e.g., OpenTelemetry) provides latency breakdowns. This slide sets up the scenario walkthroughs.

slides.title: Scenario 1: Microservice Deployment Evaluation
bullets: Walkthrough: identify bottleneck, correlate logs, propose fix
Outcome: error budget exhausted, rollback triggered
slides.notes: Live walkthrough: The evaluator provides a scenario. We demonstrate evaluating deployment metrics for a 3-service order system (API gateway, order service, payment service). We examine dashboards, find payment service p99 latency spike due to downstream database contention. Correlate with deployment event. Show how error budget burn triggers automated rollback. This demonstrates the evaluation skill.

slides.title: Scenario 2: AI Model Serving Pipeline Evaluation
bullets: Given: Model serving with pre/post processing
Metrics: prediction latency p99 1.2s, drift detection alerts
Walkthrough: trace through preprocess, inference, postprocess
Outcome: identify preprocessing bottleneck, scale horizontally
slides.notes: Second scenario: an AI model serving pipeline with preprocessing, inference, and postprocessing. Metrics show prediction latency SLO breach and data drift alerts. We trace a request, find preprocessing step taking 600ms due to inefficient tokenization. Demonstrate horizontal scaling of preprocessing workers and model batching. Show how drift detection integrates with deployment pipeline.

slides.title: Metric Collection and Observability Stack
slides.notes: Observability stack is essential for metric evaluation. Prometheus pulls metrics from exporters. Grafana visualizes. OpenTelemetry provides vendor-neutral tracing. Logs complement metrics. Alerting rules encode SLOs. This stack enables the live evaluation demonstrated in scenarios.

slides.title: Automated Evaluation Pipelines: Continuous Validation
slides.notes: Automated evaluation pipelines continuously validate deployments. Canary analysis compares new version metrics against baseline. Automated rollback protects users. Chaos engineering injects failures to test resilience. Synthetic transactions monitor critical paths. Feedback loop informs developers. This closes the reliability loop.

slides.title: Complexity Backpressure and Its Impact on Reliability
bullets: AI agents generate complex code under pressure
slides.notes: Based on C3, complexity backpressure occurs when AI coding agents produce increasingly complex code under tight deadlines, leading to higher failure rates. Tracking code complexity metrics in CI/CD provides early warning. Automated refactoring or human review can relieve pressure. This connects to reliability metric evaluation.

slides.title: Hands-On: Instrument and Evaluate a Sample Project
bullets: Add Prometheus metrics to each service
Evaluate against given SLOs, propose improvements
slides.notes: Students work on their development machines. They instrument a sample project (e.g., a simple AI pipeline with model serving and preprocessing). They deploy locally, generate load, and use Grafana dashboards to evaluate deployment and reliability metrics against predefined SLOs. They document findings and propose improvements. This activity directly practices CO4.LO3.

slides.title: Check: Metric Selection for AI Model Serving

quiz.question: Which metric is most critical for detecting model serving performance degradation in real-time?
options: CPU utilization of the model server
quiz.explanation: Prediction latency p99 directly reflects user-facing performance. CPU utilization is a resource metric but doesn't guarantee latency SLOs. Model parameters and training loss are offline metrics, not deployment metrics.

slides.notes: This check assesses understanding of deployment vs offline metrics. The most tempting wrong answer is CPU utilization because it's commonly monitored but doesn't capture tail latency.

slides.title: Check: Reliability Evaluation Decision

quiz.question: During a canary deployment, the error budget burn rate exceeds 10x. What is the correct automated action?
quiz.explanation: A burn rate >10x indicates rapid error budget consumption. Automated rollback protects users. Pausing and alerting is slower. Increasing traffic worsens impact. Ignoring violates SLO commitments.

slides.notes: This check tests knowledge of error budget policies and automated remediation. The tempting wrong answer is pausing and alerting, which is manual and slower than automated rollback.

slides.title: Key Takeaways: Deployment and Reliability Metric Evaluation
bullets: Deployment metrics: latency, throughput, errors, rollbacks
Reliability metrics: MTBF, MTTR, SLOs, error budgets
Live scenario walkthroughs demonstrate evaluation skill
slides.notes: Summarize the lecture: We covered core deployment and reliability metrics, how to evaluate them for multi-component AI-native systems, and walked through two live scenarios. We introduced the observability stack and automated evaluation pipelines. The hands-on activity gave practical experience. These skills are assessed in the endsem exam.
